mechanism: Deucravacitinib is an oral selective allosteric tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) inhibitor that binds the TYK2 regulatory domain and inhibits receptor-mediated TYK2/STAT signaling involved in IL-23, type I interferon, and downstream psoriasis inflammatory pathways.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists POETYK PSO-LTE (NCT04036435) as an active, not recruiting Phase 3 open-label extension with actual enrollment of 1,466, estimated primary completion July 25, 2026, and estimated study completion July 26, 2026. SOTYKTU is FDA-approved and marketed for adult moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and active psoriatic arthritis.
expected_launch_window: Already launched in the U.S. in September 2022; not a pipeline launch
clinical_summary: SOTYKTU is a first-in-class oral TYK2 inhibitor for adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. FDA labeling shows superiority to placebo and apremilast in PSO-1 and PSO-2 at Week 16: PASI 75 was 58% and 53% for SOTYKTU versus 13% and 9% for placebo, and 35% and 40% for apremilast. BMS reported five-year LTE data with maintained responses among continuously treated patients entering the LTE: PASI 75 67.3%, PASI 90 46.3%, and sPGA 0/1 52.6% at Year 5. Differentiation is meaningful versus older oral options, but this packet should not be treated as a future pipeline launch because the product is already marketed.
safety_summary: Label warnings include hypersensitivity, infections, tuberculosis screening, malignancies including lymphomas, rhabdomyolysis/elevated CPK, triglyceride and liver-enzyme abnormalities, avoidance of live vaccines, and potential risks related to JAK inhibition. In PSO-1/PSO-2 through Week 16, common adverse reactions more frequent than placebo included upper respiratory infections 19.2%, increased CPK 2.7%, herpes simplex 2.0%, mouth ulcers 1.9%, folliculitis 1.7%, and acne 1.4%; discontinuation due to adverse reactions was 2.4% versus 3.8% for placebo. BMS reported no new safety signals at five years in more than 5,000 patient-years of exposure.
management_tools: Exclude from pipeline-launch watchlists for psoriasis because SOTYKTU is already FDA-approved and marketed
Step requirement or documentation of inadequate response, intolerance, or contraindication to traditional systemic psoriasis therapy where plan design permits
Specialist prescribing requirement or consultation with dermatology
Continuation criteria requiring documented clinical response after initial authorization period
Quantity limit aligned to labeled dose of one 6 mg tablet daily
Concurrent-use edit against biologics, other targeted synthetic oral agents, or potent immunosuppressants when not supported by label or policy
evidence_gaps: ClinicalTrials.gov has no posted results for NCT04036435 despite long-term extension data being available through publications and company presentations.
The cost estimate uses public cash price for 30 tablets and does not reflect negotiated rebates, channel mix, patient assistance, or plan-specific net cost.
Comparative effectiveness versus newer high-efficacy biologics and emerging oral psoriasis agents is not fully resolved by the PSO-1/PSO-2 apremilast-controlled pivotal trials.
The label was expanded to active psoriatic arthritis in March 2026; this packet focuses on psoriasis but utilization management may need to account for indication spillover.

sources.title: Inflammatory Conditions - Sotyktu Prior Authorization Policy
supports: Prior authorization is recommended for prescription benefit coverage of Sotyktu.

Initial plaque psoriasis approval requires adult age, traditional systemic therapy trial or methotrexate contraindication, no concurrent potent immunosuppressants, and dermatologist prescribing or consultation.
Continuation requires at least 3 months on therapy, beneficial clinical response, symptom improvement, and no concurrent potent immunosuppressants.
Policy lists concurrent use with a biologic or targeted synthetic oral small molecule drug as not medically necessary.

expected_launch_window.value: Already launched in the U.S. in September 2022; not a pipeline launch
expected_launch_window.method: Used FDA approval date and BMS launch-availability statement instead of forecasting from the long-term extension trial.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The assigned record is a long-term extension for a product already approved for the requested psoriasis indication, so it should be flagged as a marketed-product exclusion rather than modeled as a future pipeline asset.

annual_cost_range.method: Applied labeled dosing of one 6 mg tablet daily to the public 30-tablet price: $6,977.91 per 30 tablets x 12 fills = $83,734.92, rounded to $83,735.
annual_cost_range.explanation: The estimate reflects public gross drug price only and excludes rebates, dispensing fees, patient assistance, adherence gaps, labs, visits, or adverse-event costs.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted first-in-class oral TYK2 mechanism, pivotal superiority over placebo and apremilast, and durable five-year LTE data against the availability of injectable high-efficacy biologics.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: SOTYKTU offers an oral targeted option with stronger efficacy than apremilast in pivotal trials and durable long-term data, but it is not a new pipeline entrant and does not displace biologic management outright.

budget_impact.method: Assessed annual gross cost near $84k, chronic dosing, large psoriasis eligible population, existing market availability, and standard specialty pharmacy controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient cost is material, but the product is already on the market and can be managed through established psoriasis specialty-drug controls rather than launch-readiness work.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from already-approved status, existing payer criteria, oral pharmacy-benefit routing, and lack of a pending psoriasis launch event from NCT04036435.
disruption_risk.explanation: The main action is data hygiene and continued management, not a new pipeline disruption response.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects marketed-product exclusion concern, current managed availability, and ongoing LTE/label updates.
recommended_action.explanation: Remove from prospective psoriasis pipeline launch planning, keep standard PA/quantity/continuation controls current, and monitor long-term safety plus psoriatic arthritis utilization effects.

quality_flags: Marketed/approved product study: SOTYKTU (deucravacitinib; BMS-986165) was FDA-approved for adult moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis on 2022-09-09 and launched in September 2022, so NCT04036435 should not be treated as a future psoriasis pipeline asset.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04036435 is an active, not recruiting long-term extension with no posted results, while long-term results are available through company releases and publications.
The public price estimate is gross and does not represent payer net cost after rebates or patient assistance.
SOTYKTU labeling was revised in March 2026 to include active psoriatic arthritis; this may affect utilization management even though the requested indication is psoriasis.
